faq.question: What's her name and does she have a nickname?
faq.answer: Her full name is Christine Woolf, but she also goes by Cici! She's a Senior Software Engineer passionate about building secure, scalable web and mobile applications with modern technologies like React, React Native, Next.js, and Node.js.

faq.question: What technologies does she work with?
faq.answer: She works with React and React Native for frontend/mobile development, Next.js for full-stack web applications, Node.js and GoLang for backend services, and modern tools like Auth0, New Relic, Three.js, and Tailwind CSS. She has specialized experience with authentication/authorization systems, AI-assisted development workflows, performance monitoring, and IoT data platforms.

faq.question: What's her current role?
faq.answer: She's a Senior Software Engineer at Capillary Technologies, where she designs and owns the authorization framework for a healthcare platform with React Native mobile and Next.js web clients. She won 1st place in the company's AI hackathon and has cut delivery time by ~30% using AI-assisted development practices. She was promoted from Software Engineer to Senior Software Engineer after 7 months.

faq.question: What kind of projects does she build?
faq.answer: She focuses on building secure, compliant web and mobile applications. Recent work includes greenfield healthcare platforms with PHI handling, authorization frameworks using Auth0, identity resolution layers, and production monitoring dashboards. She also builds interactive portfolios, IoT data platforms, and AI-powered applications. She has particular experience with complex authentication flows and real-time systems.

faq.question: What's her experience with authentication and security?
faq.answer: She designed and owns the authorization framework for Capillary's web and mobile applications under regulatory compliance. This includes Auth0 integration, PKCE flow, JWT tokens, session cookies, and Next.js BFF pattern. She also handles PHI (Protected Health Information) and HIPAA compliance requirements, including identity resolution and sensitive data access patterns.

faq.question: What's her experience with AI?
faq.answer: She won 1st place of 20 teams in Capillary's company-wide AI hackathon as the sole engineer. She's reduced ticket delivery time by ~30% using AI-assisted development practices, built reusable AI-assisted developer workflows, and created guides that help engineers build, test, and release correctly. She's also integrated OpenAI GPT-4 into her portfolio for an intelligent chatbot.

faq.question: How can I contact her?
faq.answer: You can connect with her on LinkedIn at https://www.linkedin.com/in/christinewoolf/

faq.question: What's her development approach?
faq.answer: She believes in writing clean, maintainable code with a focus on security, performance, and user experience. She prioritizes automated testing, comprehensive documentation, and collaborative development. She actively supports her team through code review, builds reusable tooling, and leverages AI-assisted workflows to improve productivity. Her experience spans from IoT systems requiring high reliability to healthcare platforms requiring strict compliance.

faq.question: What's her background before programming?
faq.answer: She has a diverse background in languages, philosophy, and music. She studied in Germany, conducted research in Guatemala, and taught ESL while traveling through Central and South America. This international experience and multilingual background brings unique perspectives to her development work, especially in building accessible, global applications.

faq.question: What's her working style like?
faq.answer: She's deeply focused and methodical. You'll often find her at her desk fully immersed in problem-solving for hours with Bose headphones playing quiet music. She takes a research-first approach - diving deep into documentation and technical resources before implementation. She loves creating diagrams and visual documentation to discuss technical approaches with colleagues, preferring to map out architecture and flows visually before coding.
